memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But the Israelites were unfaithful in regard to the devoted things; Achan son of Karmi, the son of Zimri, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of them. So the Lord's anger burned against Israel. — Josh 7:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After the glorious victory at Jericho comes a sobering "but." One man, Achan, secretly took some of the devoted things God had strictly forbidden. Nobody saw it. No one in the camp knew. Yet notice how the verse reads: "the Israelites were unfaithful," and "the Lord's anger burned against Israel." One man sinned in secret, and the whole nation was affected.

This is a hard truth we would rather avoid: sin is never as private as we imagine. We tell ourselves, "This only concerns me; it hurts no one else." But we belong to one another. Achan's hidden greed brought consequences on his whole community. Our choices, even the secret ones, ripple outward and touch the people around us.

Notice also that God saw what no human eye could see. Achan may have fooled the entire camp, but he could not hide from God. "Nothing in all creation is hidden from God's sight" (Heb 4:13). What we bury in secret is fully known to Him.

This chapter is placed right after Jericho for a reason. The greatest danger to God's people came not from the walled city outside, but from the sin hidden within. Our fiercest battles are often internal. Thankfully, the answer to hidden sin is not hidden striving but honest confession, for "if we confess our sins, he is faithful and just and will forgive us" (1 John 1:9). What we cannot hide, we can bring into the light of God's mercy in Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you treat some sins as "private," forgetting how they affect others?
2. Is there something hidden in your life that God already fully sees?
3. How does the promise of forgiveness free you to bring hidden things into the light?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You see what no one else can see. Give me courage to bring my hidden sins into Your light, and thank You for the cleansing I have in Christ. Amen.
